conclusion: The nominal longer reproduction strongly beat the shortened warmup, rejecting the idea that shortening warmup was harmless. Multiple schedule lengths changed together; this is a regimen-level control, not a clean single warmup-duration estimate.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Test whether shortening random warmup to 1.024M steps avoids the prior regression while retaining slight non-defense-biased shaping.

results_insights.insight: The shortened run ended at 32.5% average win rate.
The offensive-X matchup collapsed, with paired episode length 5.01 moves.
The 1% offensive-X result came in very short games.

reasoning: The shorter warmup/overall horizon did not produce broad competence by 4.096M steps.
Very short offensive-X games indicate rapid losses rather than merely long draws.
Warmup duration, mask horizon, and total steps changed together, so this run cannot isolate warmup length alone.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Run the nominal longer-warmup same-configuration control against the shortened predecessor.

results_insights.insight: The longer control exceeded the shortened run by 23.17 percentage points.
Worst rate improved slightly from 1% to 2%.
Offensive-X recovered from 1% to 94%, with 5.04-move average episodes.
Comparable short episode length but radically different win rate supports a learned tactical difference.

reasoning: The longer warmup/horizon control strongly outperformed the shortened run, especially offensive-X.
More total optimization and longer masking may be as important as random warmup itself.
The three schedule horizons moved together, so the evidence supports the package rather than a clean warmup-only causal effect.
